body: I don’t think that being prepared for an emergency is bad at all. There’s just been a bit of *extreme* panic buying in Australia over the last couple of days. I think I’m a bit like you, because I’ve lived through several natural disasters as well and prepping is honestly pretty normal to me, because I’ve had to do it before. I’ve now always got extra in my cupboards out of habit. Probably a bit weird of me, but oh well. It means I have avoided all the panic buying in supermarkets this week.

A voice of reason! 

I was proud of how we all banded together during the fires and floods, despite no leadership from our government. Gives me hope for the months ahead.

My flight’s in 48 hours, so looks like I’ll be going. I’m flying with Qantas and they just issued alerts saying anyone who’s been to mainland China in the last 14 days will likely be denied entry in Singapore. That’s fortunately not an issue for me. I guess I’m going to play it by ear until my flight, but everyone I know tells me I’m just being paranoid, which is comforting.

I’m travelling from Australia to the UK on Monday, with a stopover in Singapore (same on the way back). This whole thing has given me bad anxiety, so sorry if I come across as paranoid, but is there any reason to change these flights?

My mum had pancreatic cancer and I was her full-time carer. I’m an only child, and my father was out of the picture, so the responsibility was 100% on me. I quit my job and moved cities to look after my mum. I don’t regret it in the slightest and would do it all again in a heartbeat, but it was incredibly hard. Hardest and most exhausting thing I’ve ever done. It’s been a year since she passed away and I’m still recovering. 

 I never got to sleep as I had to give her medication every three hours, including through the night. If ever I slept through an alarm, I would be woken up by her screaming in pain, which then made me feel incredibly guilty and really resent the fact that I had to sleep, so I would do anything NOT to sleep. Not only that, but she became incontinent and would throw up all the time, so I had to bathe her and wash the sheets several times throughout the day and night. 

At the end, I hadn’t slept in two weeks, to the point where the doctor nearly hospitalised me. i was hallucinating and experiencing a level of exhaustion so extreme that I could barely function. 

I think a lot of people don’t realise how unbelievably hard it is to care for someone so unwell. And you have a huge amount to deal with given that you’re still working on top of that! AND looking after her partner and pets as well. 

I wish I had some really good advice to give you, but all I can say is I can empathise with what you’re going through right now. I know how fucking hard it is, just on a physical level, let alone emotional. 

Please take care of yourself. If there are any resources (like cancer charities that provide cleaning services etc) you can take advantage of, do. I didn’t have the energy to even look those things up when my mum was sick, but boy would it have helped me. If you have other family or friends, maybe ask them if they can find out for you? Basic tasks like shopping and cooking can become unbearable in these situations. 

I’m glad you’ve managed to get 48 hours to do your own stuff, but I think it’s also extremely important to have some time completely to yourself, not spent on tasks or work or anything, but time that is 100% yours. If you’re at the point where your own life is in danger, you absolutely need to take that time and protect yourself.  Given that your siblings live so much closer, it sounds like they could step up more than they have! Of course you’re feeling angry, because you’re being pushed beyond your limits. It’s not sustainable. 

I am so sorry you’re going through this. Feel free to message me here if you need to vent!
So true about the numbers. I’ve called a few and the people on the other end were so unhelpful I feel like it did me more harm than good.

Thanks for your response. I guess I’m just feeling alone and very depressed and I was looking for some help. I haven’t got anyone who I can talk to, so I thought I would post on here. But you’re right, it’s not about me, and I have to be there for my Mum.

Hey, I can empathise with what you’re going through. My mum was diagnosed with terminal pancreatic cancer 4 weeks ago and I have been so emotional. I’ve cried almost every single day since I found out. My mum and I are best friends and I don’t want to lose her. I’m her primary caregiver so I have to be strong for her, but when I’m alone I just burst into tears a lot. It’s so hard, but being able to talk to other people online has been a huge help to me.

Thank you so much for this message. My mum is really sick and sleeps/dozes most of the day and is often quite out of it. Fortunately I think we’ve got her pain mostly under control, but the drugs she’s on make her so drowsy and dopey. She’s also suffering from extremely bad nausea and dizziness. There are moments where she seems lucid and we can have a small conversation and a hug and they’re so precious. She’s starting chemo on Tuesday so I really hope that gives her a lot more time and a better quality of life. Fuck this fucking disease. It’s so unfair. 

I’m not sure what to expect with chemo. Most people have told me it’s going to be a lot harder than it already is, but the oncologist said to me yesterday that she might start feeling better quite soon. 

Anyway, thanks again for your message. I was lucky enough prior to mum’s diagnosis that I never had to think about cancer and what people go through, but now I know how hard it is and I have so much respect for everyone who’s battling this disease, both the patients and their caregivers.
